newsitem.title: UK: Eurostar breakdown ends Channel tunnel misery year.
newsitem.headline: Eurostar breakdown ends Channel tunnel misery year.

text.p: The operators of high-speed Eurostar trains through the Channel tunnel put on a brave face on Tuesday after a London-Paris express was stranded in the tunnel overnight, further tarnishing the system's safety record.
In what Eurostar called an unprecedented incident, both engines on an inter-city train carrying 469 passengers failed in the middle of the 32 mile (51 km) tunnel on Monday evening.
"It was a power failure -- we're still waiting to find out why it happened," a Eurostar spokesman said by telephone. The disabled train was being inspected in a Paris depot, he added.

Schedules returned to normal on Tuesday and Eurostar said the incident, and sub-zero temperatures across much of Europe, did not appear to have put off travellers, the bulk of whom were going from London for New Year celebrations in Paris.
The breakdown was the first to occur inside the tunnel since a fire on board a freight train last month injured 34 people and closed down the link for more than two weeks.
A rapid restart of most services by operator Eurotunnel SA/Plc prompted criticism from some British members of parliament and fire brigade trade unions.
Fears were swiftly reawakened when an empty train just ouside the British end of the link caught fire after an electrical fault a fortnight ago.
For debt-laden Eurotunnel, 1996 has also been a year characterised by continuing financial headaches.

Although the company managed to settle an outline debt-for-equity swap with its 225 banks in October, creating a plan to pay off its 8.7 billion pound ($14.7 billion) debt mountain, long-suffering shareholders felt it gave them little.
The company's shares in London were set to end 1996 just under 80 pence, compared with their 1995 close of 87 pence.
While Eurotunnel stock has dropped 8.0 percent in the year, the London market as a whole has risen by about 12 percent.
In Paris, the firm's equivalent French shares were set to end 1996 at about 7.0 francs, just above their 1995 finish of 6.65 francs. ($1=.5920 Pound)
